styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Ming tombs, city walls and the old capital's museums.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, Confucius market lanes and riverside evenings.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Duck, dumplings and cheap street snacks all day.

stays.why: City centre. Metro interchange, malls and easy rides to most sights.
Confucius Temple lanes, river views and snack streets on your doorstep. Livelier and noisier at night.
Quiet, green and near the lake, city wall and railway station. Good for walks and slower evenings.
Best for early high-speed trains and the S1 airport line. Fewer sights within walking distance.

food: Try Nanjing salted duck (yanshui ya) and duck blood and vermicelli soup. Both are local staples.
Fuzimiao and Laomendong lanes are good for snacking: dumplings, tangbao soup buns and sweet rice cakes.
Look for small local noodle and duck shops off the main streets; a simple meal often costs ¥15–40.
Book a proper sit-down dinner for Jiangsu cuisine; expect roughly ¥60–150 per person, more in hotel restaurants.
Drink tea at a teahouse near the Confucius Temple area. Check prices first; tourist spots can be pricey.
more_time: Add a half day at the Ming Xiaoling tomb and Purple Mountain area; combine with the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum if you have energy.
Take a day trip by high-speed train to Suzhou or Yangzhou; check times and prices on the day.
Spend an afternoon at the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall; it is sobering and needs quiet time. Check opening hours and booking rules on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Ming tombs, city wall and Fuzimiao food lanes without rushing; add a night for a day trip.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 8°C, lows near 0°C. Pack a warm coat.
Still cold, highs around 11°C. Fewer rain days, good for museums.
Milder spring: highs near 16°C, lows around 7°C. Layer up.
Pleasant spring, highs near 21°C. Good walking weather.
Warm and green, highs near 26°C. Light rain gear helps.
Hot start to summer, highs near 29°C. Expect about 12 rain days.
Hottest and wettest: highs near 31°C, lows near 25°C, 17 rain days.
Still hot and humid, highs near 32°C. Plan indoor breaks.
Cooling down, highs near 28°C. Pleasant evenings return.
Best month: highs near 22°C, lows near 14°C, fewer rain days.
Crisp autumn, highs near 17°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.
Cold again, highs near 10°C, lows near 1°C. Fewest rain days.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold, fairly dry winters and hot, humid, rainy summers. Spring and autumn are the best times to walk.

items.title: Best time: April, May and October
items.text: Highs around 21–26°C and comfortable lows. Ideal for the city wall, Purple Mountain and lake walks.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 29–32°C with muggy nights around 21–25°C. Do outdoor sights early morning.

items.title: Rain peaks in July
items.text: About 17 rain days in July and 12–13 in June and August. Carry a light rain jacket or umbrella.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs around 8–11°C and lows near 0–1°C. Bring a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Dry, clear autumn
items.text: October and November have fewer rain days and mild highs. Great for photos and long walks.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a warm coat for winter, breathable clothes and rain gear for summer. Comfortable shoes for cobbled lanes.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; Didi or taxi for late nights and door-to-door rides.

modes.text: Clean, cheap and fast. Single tokens cost ¥2–9 and run roughly 05:00–23:00. Line S1 links Nanjing South Station to the airport in about 30 min for ¥6.
City buses cost a flat ¥2 (some ¥1). An IC card gives about 20% off.
Taxis start at ¥9 plus a ¥2 service fee; most trips cost under ¥25. Didi works well, but drivers rarely speak English, so show Chinese addresses.
Not needed in the city; metro, buses and taxis cover the sights. Skip it unless you plan trips outside Nanjing.
Good in spring and autumn for Fuzimiao lanes, the city wall and lake paths. Hot and humid in summer, so walk early or late.
Hello and Meituan bikes are everywhere. Handy for short hops between metro stops and sights.
Trams serve the southwest and Qilin Town. Useful only if your plans go that way.
